title: 'Bloos' for Norman Granz's Jazz Scene
summary: Written in 1947-48 and released years later, it was one side of Granz's carte blanche album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: After 1955, after
"Here's George", then came "Bloos". "Bloos" is a very special thing all on its own; is it not?
"Bloos" was done--
To the transcriber, that's capital B-L-O-O-S.
--that was done during the Raeburn days. That was written in '47--'48 but it wasn't released until 1952 or '51, I think. It was recorded years before.
I'm sorry, I was misremembering that, it was recorded during your Raeburn days?
Yeah, I was still with Boyd when I did that. I wrote it, I think, in '47. I don't think it was released until '51--
(Side A of Tape 5 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
That was for Norman Grant?
Right.
It was an album called "The Jazz Scene"--is that the first you knew of it, when I sent it to you?
It's the first I've heard of it. I knew it existed.
Oh, you heard of it before that.
I don't think I heard it.
Did you see the album here?
Yes.
Then you know what the album is and who is involved with it?
Yes.

Norman went to each of the people and said, I'm making this record, this album and I want to give each of you people a side on the twelve inch record, carte blanche. If you went fifty men, fifty violins, a symphony, you've got it. If you want to go in the studio alone and just sit at the piano, you've got it.
If you want to do it with a string quartet, anything, carte blanche, anything.
He'll release anything you do?
He said that to everybody there.
